summary: John Vincent Bellezza is a tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2014.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and tibetology, John W. Pettit completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman. He also studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder, working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon, completing his PhD under Don Levi. He taught at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.

John W. Spellman was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from ~1957 to 1960. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (~1967–2000).

John Watson McCrindle was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned a B.A. and LL.D. from the University of Edinburgh. He served as Principal of Doveton College and Patna College, Professor at Krishnagar Government College, and Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
John Wenger was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bern in 1827 and at the University of Rhode Island around 1878, receiving a D.D.

John Whalen-Bridge is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from the University of Connecticut, UC Davis, and USC. He served as Gaikokujin-kiyoshi at the University of the Ryukyus and Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore.

John Whaley Watson was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist who served in the Bombay Staff Corps (~1861–1889). He was President of the Rajasthik Court in Kathiawar (~1873–1886) and political agent for the Kathiawar Agency (1881–1889).

John William Neill was an Indology scholar who studied at King's College London and the University of Edinburgh. He served as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta, Professor and Lecturer at University College London, and Reader at SOAS.

John Wilson, an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, Superintendent of the Free Church of Scotland Mission, and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai.
John Zephaniah Holwell was an Indology scholar who studied surgery at Guy's Hospital. He became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1767.

Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Jōchō Chihaya. He held posts at Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, the Japan Academy, and served as head of Horyu-ji from 1903 to 1950.
Joji Fujii is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University from around 1966 to 1974. He later held a post at Kyoto University from approximately 1989 to 2012.

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He held faculty posts at Shuchiin University and Otemae University (~1966–1994).

Jon Holt is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington. He was appointed Professor of Japanese at Portland State University in 2010.

Jon Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT, training under Jack Kornfield, Joseph Goldstein, Philip Kapleau, Thich Nhat Hanh, and Seungsahn Haengwon. He served as Professor of Medicine Emeritus at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford, completing a D.Phil. under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held professorships at Sussex, Monash, New York University, and the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. He held faculty posts at Western Michigan University, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who earned his BA from Amherst College and PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Vermont, Drew University, and Princeton University.

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed doctoral work in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1976–1986). He also served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.
